description:
Real ownership. Real impact. Build from day one.

Are you an ambitious graduate ready to tackle complex, real-world challenges at the intersection of data, strategy and tech? 

The Future Leaders Graduate Program – Business Analytics at Picnic is a two-year launchpad for exceptional talents. From day one, you join a business team, own a business topic, and become an expert in your field.

At Picnic, we’re building the future of grocery. Using cutting-edge technology and data-driven innovation, we challenge the status quo and build the world’s smartest, most customer-focused supermarket.
We move fast, think big, and turn bold ideas into tangible impact.

Tricks of the trade

  • Lead with ambition: Bring your relentless determination, creativity, and grit. Take the driver’s seat and redefine the grocery shopping experience for millions. You will be expected to think independently, move fast, and deliver results.
  • Steep learning curve: Your growth comes from owning real problems, testing your ideas, learning from your mistakes and starting again. You'll blend hands-on training with immediate execution, you’ll move at a pace that accelerates your growth like nowhere else.
  • Solve real-life puzzles: Spot opportunities, use tools at the forefront of technology, and own the outcome end to end. Not just making slides, but building the solution yourself.
  • Innovate across borders: You’ll collaborate with teams across the Netherlands, Germany, and France, tackling challenges that redefine how Picnic operates at a European scale.
  • High-performance environment: You’ll work alongside some of the best teams in analytics and tech, people who set a high bar and expect you to do the same.

From learning to leading

 

Throughout the two-year program, you’ll own business-critical projects from start to finish, supported by mentorship, learning sessions, and regular feedback.

You’ll strengthen your leadership skills in project management, storytelling, stakeholder communication, and giving and receiving feedback, while sharpening your technical skills in Python, SQL, Excel, and PowerPoint.

As your scope grows, so does your responsibility. You might scale your initial project or take on new challenges within the same domain. Either way, the pace is yours to set, and there’s always a new challenge to lead and an opportunity to make an impact. That’s why every journey is unique: there’s no standardized path through the program, just continuous opportunities to learn, and lead.

 

Where you’ll make an impact

From day one, you’ll be embedded in a business team, taking ownership in one of the following domains:

  • Consumer - Drive growth through pricing, supplier strategy, and our market strategy. Think: Shaping our successful market entry into new cities. Your decisions shape how millions of customers experience Picnic.
  • Logistics - Build the backbone of Picnic: robotic fulfilment, demand forecasting, route optimization across Europe and much more

Your superpowers

You don't wait for permission. You see a problem, build the solution, and bring people with you, before anyone asks. You've probably already started something: a project, a product, a business, an initiative that didn't exist until you made it happen.

More specifically, you:

  • Are about to graduate (or recently graduated) a Masters in a quantitative field
  • Have experience in high-performance environments: consulting, fast-growth startups, or competitive internships.
  • Show an entrepreneurial mindset: you build, improve, and take ownership without being asked
  • Think like a builder: hands-on, curious, and driven to challenge the status quo with practical solutions
  • You have already gained basic knowledge in PowerPoint, Python, SQL, Excel or alternative coding languages 
  • EU citizenship or valid EU working permit required.

Many strong candidates (particularly women) talk themselves out of applying because they don't tick every box. If this excites you and you believe you have what it takes, apply. We only hire when we find the right match. That’s why our selection process is intentionally highly selective.

 Why Picnic?

  • Grow as we grow. We’re scaling quickly across countries and millions of customers and this is just the start. Grow your impact as we grow; we invest in your path but the driver's seat is always yours.
  • Work with other innovators. Work with a driven, energetic team that builds, wins, and celebrates together (think of legendary Friday drinks, our Ski trip and our parties)
  • Kickstart your career. Earn a competitive salary and step into a program designed to launch your long-term future at Picnic.

When are you joining? 

  • Fall Edition 2026
    Start dates: September, October
    *earlier or later dates can be arranged, please indicate your preference in the application question
  • Spring Edition 2027
    Start dates: February, March
    *earlier or later dates can be arranged, please indicate your preference in the application question

📍 Location: Full-time in Paris, with period trips to NL and DE

There is no deadline: Our aim is to find the most ambitious people out there. We onboard talents on a monthly basis, so whether you join in April or August, you’ll always have a group of people sharing the ride. 

 

Picnic Perks

🚲Health and Transportation
Through our partnerships with Malakoff Humanis and OpenUp, you have the opportunity to enroll in our company health insurance plan, as well as free and easy access to professional psychologists, workshops, and practical tools. Additionally, if you commute to work using public transportation, we reimburse 50% of your subscription cost.

🍉Food
Since we are located in the center of Paris, there is no on-site cafeteria. However, you will receive meal vouchers worth €11 per day to explore all the delicious restaurants nearby. Our small kitchen is also stocked with tasty snacks and refreshments.

📈Personal and Professional Development
You will have the opportunity to develop your skills not only through exciting projects and a dynamic environment but also via training programs offered by Lepaya.

🏖️All the rest
You get 25 days of paid vacation, plus additional rest days (RTT) based on the number of days worked in the year. Picnic provides you with a laptop, a phone, and a paid SIM card.
🚀Access to exclusive deals and perks through our Works Council (CSE) and our partner Swile (gift cards, concert tickets, cinema discounts, and more)

FAQ

Do I need a quantitative background? It's a strong advantage, but not a hard requirement. If your internships and projects demonstrate real hands-on ownership and data-driven thinking, we'll consider your application. You do need a Master's degree, basic knowledge of Python or SQL, and relevant work experience.

Does the program include rotations? No, intentionally. We believe depth creates ownership, and ownership creates impact. Rather than rotating across teams, you’ll go deep in one area, build real expertise, and gradually expand your scope as your impact grows. If you have topic preferences, tell us during the process.

In what language should I apply? English. Please include your CV and Master's degree transcript or any other relevant test scores (e.g., GMAT)

What are the long-term opportunities after the program? This program is a fast track into a high-impact career at Picnic, it’s an entry point for a long-term future, not a two-year stopover. 

Career paths here are as varied as the people on them. Some grow vertically, building deep expertise and a team around them as their project expands. Others move laterally - from Commercial to Fulfilment, Distribution to Customer, or wherever their strengths and ambitions take them. What they share is real ownership, real impact, and a career they shaped themselves.

Our Product Team is looking for a passionate and dedicated colleague to join them and build world-class products to move the performance marketing industry forward.

  • You will identify opportunities with product peers to further add value to our plugins and various platform integrations

  • You have experience or high-level understanding of Ecommerce or similar platforms

  • You are data driven and possess analytical and problem-solving skills
  • You are comfortable in communicating with multiple stakeholders
  • You are self-motivated, organised, capable of prioritising work and focusing on important tasks

 

Our Offer

  • Collaborate across disciplines while closely working with product designers, product owners, and frontend, backend, and mobile engineers to share ideas and deliver product innovations.

  • Relevant product experience: 3+ years of experience working with customer-facing products in industries such as e-commerce, fintech, or SaaS.

  • Clear communication: Excellent English communication skills and comfort raising concerns, sharing ideas, and documenting your work.
  • Collaborative mindset: You contribute to the team, take initiative, and step in to help when needed.

Grâce à ses différentes entités expertes et sectorielles, Theodo aide ses clients à concevoir des produits innovants, à accélérer leur développement et à répondre à leurs enjeux stratégiques et opérationnels. Contexte du recrutement Dans un contexte de développement et de transformation continue, Theodo France doit poursuivre sa croissance, renforcer son excellence opérationnelle et assurer l’alignement entre ses ambitions stratégiques et leur mise en œuvre au quotidien. Pour accompagner Noémie Parker dans le pilotage de ses priorités et le développement de Theodo France, nous recherchons un(e) Chief of Staff, véritable bras droit, capable de faire le lien entre la vision stratégique, les décisions de la direction et leur exécution opérationnelle. Au plus près des enjeux de l’entreprise, tu travailleras sur des sujets transverses à fort impact, en interaction avec les équipes de direction et les responsables opérationnels. Ton rôle sera de fluidifier la prise de décision, de structurer les initiatives prioritaires et de garantir leur bonne exécution. Tes missions Ton objectif : démultiplier l’impact de Noémie Parker et contribuer directement à la performance de Theodo France, en apportant un appui stratégique et opérationnel, tout en garantissant la bonne coordination des parties prenantes. 1. Contribuer à la définition et au déploiement de la stratégie Participer à la définition des priorités stratégiques de Theodo France à 12 mois, en lien avec Noémie Parker et les équipes de direction. Analyser les leviers de croissance, les enjeux de performance et les opportunités de développement. Préparer les revues stratégiques et contribuer à la formalisation des plans d’action. Transformer les orientations stratégiques en objectifs clairs, mesurables et partagés par les équipes. 2. Accompagner la direction dans le pilotage opérationnel Préparer et animer les réunions de direction : définition de l’ordre du jour, priorisation des sujets, suivi des décisions et des actions. Structurer les processus de prise de décision et assurer le suivi des priorités. Anticiper les points de blocage et faciliter la résolution des sujets transverses. Organiser les temps forts de la direction : séminaires stratégiques, réunions d’équipe et moments de réflexion collective. Préparer les supports de communication permettant de partager la vision, les priorités et les résultats avec l’ensemble des équipes. 3. Piloter les chantiers stratégiques et transverses Identifier et structurer les projets prioritaires pour le développement de Theodo France. Définir les objectifs, les indicateurs de suivi, les responsabilités et les échéances de chaque chantier. Coordonner les parties prenantes et accompagner les responsables de projets dans leur exécution. Suivre l’avancement des initiatives, identifier les risques et proposer des plans d’action correctifs. Veiller à ce que les décisions prises par la direction se traduisent concrètement en résultats. 4. Contribuer à la performance et à l’excellence opérationnelle Analyser les indicateurs clés de performance de l’activité et identifier les axes d’amélioration. Préparer des analyses et recommandations pour éclairer les décisions de la direction. Accompagner la mise en place de nouveaux processus et outils visant à améliorer l’efficacité collective. Piloter des projets transverses à l’échelle de Theodo France, selon les priorités identifiées par la direction. Faciliter la collaboration entre les différentes équipes et entités pour accélérer l’exécution des projets. Tes perspectives En devenant Chief of Staff, tu seras au cœur des décisions et des enjeux de développement de Theodo France. Tu développeras une compréhension approfondie du fonctionnement d’une entreprise technologique, de la définition de sa stratégie à son exécution opérationnelle. Tu travailleras directement avec la direction sur des problématiques variées, avec un niveau d’exposition élevé et une forte autonomie. Ce poste te permettra de développer des compétences solides en stratégie, en pilotage de la performance, en gestion de projets complexes et en leadership transverse. À terme, cette expérience pourra ouvrir la voie à des fonctions de direction opérationnelle, de direction de business unit ou à d’autres rôles de leadership au sein d’un environnement entrepreneurial. Profil recherché Tu disposes de 3 à 6 ans d’expérience, idéalement avec une expérience significative en conseil en stratégie, en organisation ou en transformation. Tu possèdes un excellent esprit analytique et sais structurer des problématiques complexes pour en tirer des recommandations concrètes. Tu es organisé(e), rigoureux(se) et capable de gérer plusieurs sujets simultanément, sans perdre de vue les priorités. Tu es un(e) véritable doer : tu sais passer de la réflexion à l’action et obtenir des résultats concrets. Tu disposes d’un excellent relationnel et sais interagir avec des interlocuteurs variés, notamment des membres de la direction. Tu es à l’aise pour challenger les idées, formuler des recommandations et faire avancer les décisions. Tu fais preuve d’autonomie, de proactivité et d’un fort sens des responsabilités. Tu apprécies les environnements exigeants, dynamiques et entrepreneuriaux, dans lesquels les priorités peuvent évoluer rapidement. Ce qui fera la différence : ta capacité à combiner hauteur de vue stratégique, rigueur d’exécution et intelligence relationnelle pour transformer les ambitions de Theodo France en résultats tangibles. Pourquoi rejoindre Theodo ? L’environnement: 💼 Rejoindre un groupe de 750 personnes avec de nombreuses possibilités d’évolutions cross-entités 🤝 Chaque Theodoer est accompagné par un coach interne. description:
Your wellbeing, our mission. Join a company shaping a healthier world.

GET TO KNOW US

At Wellhub we're revolutionizing workplace wellness. Our platform connects employees worldwide to the best partners for fitness, mindfulness, therapy, nutrition, and sleep—all in one simple subscription. Headquartered in NYC with team members in Europe, North America and South America, we’re on a mission to make every company a wellness company.

We believe work should be fulfilling, inspiring, and balanced. Here, you’ll find a team that values wellbeing, collaboration, and different perspectives, where passion and creativity push boundaries to create real impact. Your contributions will help shape a healthier, more balanced world for you and millions of people globally. 

Join us in redefining the future of wellbeing!

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

We are hiring a Senior Enterprise Client Success Manager to join our Client Success team in London.

Client Success at Wellhub plays a critical role in ensuring our largest and most strategic enterprise clients successfully adopt, scale, and extract measurable value from our wellbeing solutions. In this role, you will manage a portfolio of complex enterprise accounts, owning the post-sale relationship and driving client retention, engagement, and commercial outcomes.

This is a hands-on, client-facing role suited for someone who is comfortable managing complexity, building strong stakeholder relationships, and working cross-functionally to deliver impact. The role is hybrid, with an expectation to be in the office 2x per week.

YOUR IMPACT

  • Own the post-sale lifecycle for a portfolio of large enterprise clients, acting as the primary point of contact and ensuring long-term partnership success.
  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with HR, Reward, and Wellbeing stakeholders across complex client organisations.
  • Drive client adoption, engagement, and retention by translating client goals into clear success and engagement plans.
  • Lead renewals and support expansion opportunities within your portfolio, clearly articulating value and impact.
  • Use data and insights to monitor performance, identify risks, and recommend improvements to client strategy.
  • Collaborate closely with internal teams (Wellbeing Engagement, Operations, Customer Experience, User Growth, Partnerships, Commercial) to ensure effective delivery.
  • Proactively identify issues and risks, clearly articulating client impact and urgency to your manager to enable timely escalation and resolution.

WHO YOU ARE

  • 8+ years of experience in Client Success, Account Management, or a similar client-facing role.
  • Experience managing mid-to-large enterprise clients in a complex, fast-paced environment.
  • Comfortable owning renewals and participating in commercial conversations with clients.
  • Strong relationship-building skills, with the ability to engage and influence senior client stakeholders.
  • Data-aware, with confidence using insights and reporting to inform decisions and conversations.
  • Highly organised, able to manage multiple accounts and priorities simultaneously.
  • A collaborative, resilient professional who remains calm and solution-oriented when navigating change and complexity.

We recognize that individuals approach job applications differently. We strongly encourage all aspiring applicants to go for it, even if they don't match the job description 100%. We welcome your application and will be delighted to explore if you could be a great fit for our team. For this specific role, please note that prior experience in driving new business growth and successfully securing significant contracts with complex organizations are mandatory requirements.

WHAT WE OFFER YOU

With thoughtful benefits, emotional wellbeing resources, and a culture that empowers you to take ownership of your role and your wellbeing, we create an environment where you can thrive in all dimensions of your life. Our benefits include:

WELLHUB:  Free Gold membership with access to onsite gyms and studios, digital fitness programs, and online wellness resources for meditation, nutrition, mental wellbeing support, and more! Add up to three family members to your plan, ensuring access to wellness for those who matter most to you.

HEALTHCARE: Health and dental insurance. 

FLEXIBLE WORK: As a Flexible First company, we offer hybrid and remote options to give you the freedom to work in a way that suits you. The model for this specific role can be discussed with your recruiter and hiring manager. We offer all employees a one-time reimbursement to set up their home office equipment and a monthly work allowance to help cover the costs of working from home. Our offices are in Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Portugal, Romania, Spain, and the UK. You can work from any office or remotely based in any of these countries.

FLEXIBLE SCHEDULE:  Flexibility for us isn’t just about where we work—it also means being able to shape how and when we get things done. Together with their leaders, employees define schedules that align with their time zones, team needs, and personal routines.

PAID TIME OFF: We know how important it is to take time away from work to recharge. Employees receive a minimum of 25 days paid holiday per year with an additional day for each year of tenure (up to 5) in addition to annual holidays (including an extra holiday on your birthday!). 

PARENTAL LEAVE: Welcoming a new child is one of the most special moments in your life. Take the time to be present and enjoy your growing family. We offer 100% paid parental leave to all new parents. Parents giving birth are eligible for an extended leave and a ramp-back period to return part-time while they get settled.  

CAREER GROWTH: Access world-class platforms, participate in interactive sessions,  build your personalized development roadmap, and explore internal opportunities. We focus on continuous learning and feedback to support your journey toward personal and professional success. 

CULTURE: You’ll join a team of passionate people who come together to break boundaries, support each other, and create a meaningful impact in workplace wellness. We win together, building trust through open communication and a culture where every perspective matters. Learn more about our shared culture and values here. 

 

Want to see what it’s really like to work here? Follow us on Instagram @lifeatwellhub and watch our team video on YouTube!

Diversity, Equity, and Belonging at Wellhub

We aim to create a collaborative, supportive, and inclusive space where everyone knows they belong. 

Wellhub is committed to creating a diverse work environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, non-disqualifying physical or mental disability, national origin, veteran status, or any other basis covered by appropriate law.

Our commitment to inclusion also extends to how we recognize and reward our people. We’re proud to be Syndio Fair Pay Certified, reflecting our ongoing dedication to equitable and fair pay practices across our global team. Read more about it here.

Questions on how we treat your personal data? See our Job Applicant Privacy Notice.

If you thrive on opening doors, building partnerships and turning opportunities into wins, this is a chance to make a visible impact as we expand our META Commercial team. We currently require our Amsterdam team to come to the office 2 - 3 days per week. Clients value Baringa’s collaborative approach and the way its teams integrate seamlessly – all working with a shared understanding of what matters most. The firm is known for its kind, curious experts who listen closely and care deeply about client success as they help clients transform energy markets, modernise financial platforms, expand telecoms and digital networks through advanced data analytics, enable digital services in government, and unlock growth in consumer sectors.

Certified as a Great Place to Work around the world, Baringa has been recognised by the Financial Times in 22 categories of its UK Leading Management Consultants rankings, and by Forbes for four consecutive years as one of the World’s Best Management Consulting Firms.

Our Data, AI, Solutions and Engineering practice are looking for Consultants, Senior Consultants and Managers to join the team. 

The interface between organisations and their data is being rebuilt. Static dashboards remain useful, but they now sit alongside conversational analytics, dynamically generated insight, analytical applications and agents embedded into operational workflows. Making these experiences valuable requires more than an LLM demo. They need trusted data and semantics, robust analytics engineering, appropriate architecture and a deep understanding of how products will be used. 

We are looking for Agentic Analytics Engineers who are strong analytics engineers first and are already applying AI to how they work. You will build analytical products using SQL, Python, semantic and metric models and modern analytics platforms, while also developing Insight Agents, conversational experiences and AI-enabled applications. If you already have substantial delivery experience in agentic analytics, generative BI or LLM-enabled insight, that is highly valuable. We do not, however, expect every strong candidate to have deployed all these capabilities extensively at enterprise scale. 

This is a hands-on engineering role. Across all grades we value people who understand how things are built and can show that they are actively experimenting with AI-enabled analytics in practice. In the UK profile, we also put significant weight on consulting and advisory credibility: working directly with clients, making sense of ambiguous problems, shaping architecture and explaining the trade-offs behind technical choices. 

What you will be doing

  • Understand the business outcome, decision or workflow that the analytical capability needs to improve, and translate that into a robust technical solution. 
  • Design and build Insight Agents, conversational analytics and AI-enabled analytical applications that connect users to trusted enterprise data and tools. 
  • Ensure that any AI is explainable and aligns with the relevant guidelines and guardrails that have been defined. 
  • Design and engineer semantic and metric models so that business definitions, dimensions and measures can be used consistently across BI, applications and AI agents. 
  • Build analytical experiences using platforms such as Microsoft Fabric / Power BI, Databricks and Snowflake, as well as custom applications and APIs where that is the right choice. 
  • Integrate insight into operational workflows through APIs, embedded analytics, applications, events and agentic patterns, including appropriate human judgement and control points. 
  • Work hands-on with SQL, Python and relevant software / platform engineering tools to build, test and deploy production-quality solutions. 
  • Design for security, reliability, observability, performance, cost and responsible use so solutions can move from prototype to sustainable enterprise capability. 
  • Prototype and refine user experiences and work closely with Decision & Insight Leads, designers and end users so generated insight is understandable and actionable. 
  • Work shoulder-to-shoulder with client engineers, architects and business teams, shaping solutions as understanding develops rather than simply implementing a fixed specification. 
  • Build reusable assets, patterns and accelerators and actively learn as the agentic analytics technology landscape evolves. 

 
Your skills and experience  

  • Excellent hands-on analytics engineering ability, with evidence of analytical or data-intensive products and capabilities you have personally designed and built. 
  • Strong SQL and Python skills, alongside sound development practices such as Git, automated testing, CI/CD, APIs and well-structured, maintainable code. 
  • Hands-on experience with one or more mainstream analytics platforms. This may come from Microsoft Fabric / Power BI, Databricks, Snowflake or comparable technologies, together with the ability to learn new platforms rather than being defined by one vendor. 
  • Strong understanding of analytical, dimensional, semantic or metric modelling and why shared business meaning is critical when insight is consumed by both people and AI. 
  • A grounded understanding of how AI is changing analytics, supported by practical experimentation with capabilities such as conversational analytics, generative BI, LLM-enabled applications or agents. We are particularly interested in candidates who have already designed or delivered these capabilities, but we do not require extensive enterprise-scale deployment experience across every area. 
  • Evidence that you already use AI practically in your day-to-day analytics or engineering work, for example to explore data, write or review code, prototype solutions, automate tasks or develop analytical products, and can explain what you have learned and where these approaches create value. 
  • Ability to make sound architecture choices across platform-native and custom approaches, including an understanding of security, explainability, cost, maintainability, performance and scale. 
  • Experience building user-facing analytical experiences or working closely enough with designers and users to make sound product and interface choices. 
  • Strong problem-solving and communication skills. For UK hiring, previous consulting experience is strongly valued, or equivalent evidence that you can work through ambiguity with clients, shape solutions and influence business and technology stakeholders. 

You may also bring 

  • Experience with Microsoft Fabric semantic models, Fabric Data Agents, Power Platform or Copilot Studio. 
  • Databricks capabilities such as lakehouse / SQL, Genie or MLflow; Snowflake and Cortex capabilities. 
  • Experience with Anthropic Claude or OpenAI APIs, MCP, A2A or comparable agent and tool integration patterns. 
  • Front-end or full-stack development and user-centred design experience, for example React / TypeScript or Figma. 
  • Cloud architecture, infrastructure as code, containerisation, DevOps / DataOps, governance, lineage or AI observability experience. 

How the opportunity flexes with experience 

Consultants will typically spend a high proportion of their time designing and building, applying strong analytics engineering foundations and demonstrating active experimentation with AI-enabled approaches. Senior Consultants will increasingly own end-to-end components and workstreams, selecting appropriate patterns and working directly with client stakeholders. Managers combine sustained engineering depth with solution architecture, team leadership and client ownership, making sound choices between conventional analytics, platform-native AI and custom agentic approaches.

  • Generous Annual Leave Policy: We recognise everyone needs a well-deserved break. We provide our employees with 5 weeks of annual leave, fully available at the start of each year. In addition to this, we have introduced our 5-Year Recharge benefit which allows all employees an additional 2 weeks of paid leave after 5 years continuous service.

At Tide, we help SMEs save time and money in the running of their businesses by not only offering business accounts and related banking services, but also a comprehensive set of highly usable and connected administrative solutions, from invoicing to accounting.

Tide facts:

  • Tide is available for UK, German and French SMEs
  • Over 2 million members globally and rapidly growing
  • Over $300 million raised in funding
  • 3,000 Tideans globally
  • We have offices in Central London, with a member support and technology centre in Sofia, Bulgaria, technology centres in Serbia, Romania, Lithuania and Hyderabad and offices in Gurugram, New Delhi, Berlin, Paris and Luxembourg

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Tide is hiring a Director of Engineering to lead the engineering organisation behind KYX (KYC and KYB). Our vision for KYX is a world where every genuine business, business owner, their team, and everyone connected to them, onboards to Tide in minutes, unlocks the products they need as they grow, and never has to think twice about their data, while we identify bad actors, stop them at the door, continuously review their activity and off-board them the moment they're found.

You will be accountable for engineering strategy, organisation and execution across three domains. Onboarding KYX covers identity and access for registration and login, due diligence policy execution and vendor orchestration across the onboarding journey, and the risk scoring and agentic AI that assesses new applicants. Continuous KYX covers ongoing due diligence through periodic and event-triggered reviews, and how business owners bring their own team members onto their account. Risk Scoring is the KYX Scoring & ML team whose models power decisions across both domains.

This role sits at the intersection of regulated risk operations, member-facing conversion and applied AI. KYX Ops and KYX Policy set the rules you build for, Second Line of Defence sets the risk appetite, and our regulators set the bar. We need someone who can raise onboarding conversion and due diligence quality while driving the cost of KYX servicing per member down, and who can scale agentic solutions into workflows where a wrong answer has consequences for a member and for Tide.

As Director of Engineering, KYX you will

description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

We are looking for a technically savvy Engineering Manager to lead the Sandpipers Team within the Marketplace Payments domain. This team owns the tooling for preventing fraudulent payments and fraudulent chargebacks. You will report to the Director of Engineering and work hand in hand with Product and Data peers.

In this position, you’ll 

  • People Leadership: Lead, coach, and grow a talented team of engineers. Build and maintain a team culture based on trust, commitment, psychological safety, and clear accountability. Conduct ongoing feedback, performance, and compensation reviews.
  • Product Discovery & Planning: Partner closely with Product Managers and the team during early-stage discovery to map out the technical strategy for future product initiatives and come up with the delivery plan.
  • Delivery: Lead the team’s delivery against the product roadmap while maintaining team's health.

About you 

  • Proven Leadership: Highly skilled at building engineering teams, hiring new talent, setting clear scope, and managing priorities to keep the team focused and motivated.
  • Engineering Foundations: Background in backend engineering (ideally handling external API structures, webhook payloads, and cross-service async communication). You are comfortable guiding technical decision-making. 
  • Excellent Communicator & Vendor Coordinator: Outstanding stakeholder management skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical ideas clearly and confidently across internal teams (Product, Compliance, Legal) and external global technology providers.

Work perks 

  • The opportunity to benefit from our share options programme
  • 25 days of paid annual leave
  • Newest MacBook models
  • Confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family
  • Frequent team-building events
  • Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture
  • Lunch benefit per working day
  • A personal monthly budget for shopping on Vinted
  • Collective Defined Contribution Pension plan
  • NS Business Card for your commute to the office by public transport
  • Company bike leasing scheme
  • Monthly budget for a flexible benefits platform
  • A dog-friendly office

Working at Vinted 

Workation policy

Better balance holidays with workdays by working remotely! Up to 90 days per year in the EU, of these, 21 days can be spent globally. For non-EU citizens, it's 21 days worldwide. This can be combined with time off for vacation or personal time.

Individual learning budget

Each year, you’ll be given a learning budget (starting at €3,000), and a total of up to 10 working days over a 2-year period to support your personal and professional development.

Hybrid work 

Our hybrid model, with 2 recommended office days a week, gives you and your team the flexibility to decide if and when you want to work from home, and when to catch up in person.

Equal opportunity

We welcome applications from everybody, regardless of your background, identity, or life experiences. Job openings come with guides, not checklists. If you’re excited about a role, but don’t identify with every point in the ‘About you’ section, apply anyway – you might still be the perfect match!

€97.800—€132.300 EUR

description: GRC Lead Edinburgh Wordsmith Legal touches everything that matters in a business: every deal, every hire, every launch, every risk. Sales runs on Salesforce. Engineering runs on GitHub. In-house legal runs on inboxes, chat threads and tools that weren’t built for it. Wordsmith is changing that. We’re building the platform in-house legal runs on. Requests from across the business come in through one front door. AI agents handle the routine work. Lawyers stay in control where judgment matters. Legal finally gets to triage by risk, not by whoever shouted loudest. We’re built for in-house teams, not law firms. Our customers want to spend less on outside counsel, not more, and we’re on their side of that equation. More than 500 companies run on Wordsmith, including Financial Times, Canva, Trip.com, Revolut, Adyen, Trustpilot, and Sage. We’ve raised $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe and others, and we’re growing fast. Our customers are some of the most demanding enterprise legal departments in the world, and they hold us to a high bar on security, privacy, and responsible AI. We're looking for a senior leader to take ownership of security and compliance as we scale. The Role GRC Leads own security and compliance at Wordsmith end-to-end — setting the strategy for IT and infrastructure security, running our certification program across SOC 2, ISO 27001, and ISO 42001, embedding responsible-AI practices into how we build and ship product, and making sure privacy and regulatory obligations (GDPR and beyond) are handled properly as we grow. This is a senior role that blends strategy and hands-on execution. You'll set multi-year direction, represent Wordsmith's security posture to executives, customers, and — as we grow — the board, and build the team, tooling, and controls the company needs at the next stage, not just maintain what exists today. What You'll Do Security Strategy & Leadership Own Wordsmith's multi-year IT security and compliance roadmap — setting priorities, budget, and tooling decisions in partnership with Engineering and company leadership. IT & Infrastructure Security Own security architecture across corporate IT and infrastructure — identity & access management, endpoint protection, and cloud/network security — and lead incident response when issues arise. Compliance & Certification Own SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001/27017/27018, and ISO 42001 end-to-end — policies, controls, audit evidence, and the audits themselves. AI Governance Run our AI governance program, including AI Impact Assessments and model/AI-vendor risk reviews, ensuring responsible, compliant AI use across the product. Privacy Operations Own privacy operations end-to-end — GDPR and other regulatory obligations, DPIAs, RoPA maintenance, sub-processor management, and Data Subject Request fulfilment. Third-Party & Vendor Risk Assess vendors and AI tools for security, privacy, and AI risk before they're adopted, and put the right contractual safeguards in place at a program level. Team & Function Building Build the people, process, and tooling the function needs as it scales — starting as the senior owner of the program today, with a mandate to build out a team as Wordsmith grows. Executive & Board Reporting Own risk and compliance reporting to leadership and, as we scale, the board — translating technical risk into business terms. Customer & Deal Support Act as the senior voice on security for enterprise deals — security questionnaires, DPAs, and our Trust Center — partnering with Sales, Customer Success, and Legal to unblock deals without cutting corners. Automation & Tooling Build lean, automation-first tooling (e.g. Vanta) for evidence collection and ongoing compliance monitoring, so the program scales without scaling headcount unnecessarily. What we're looking for Essential 8-10+ years in security, IT, or compliance roles, including a track record of owning a security or compliance function end-to-end at a fast-growing SaaS or tech company. Proven experience building or scaling a security/compliance program from an early stage — ideally including time as the sole or founding owner of the function. Deep, hands-on expertise across SOC 2, the ISO 27000 series, and ideally ISO 42001. Strong grounding in core IT security fundamentals — identity & access management, endpoint/device security, and cloud or network infrastructure security. Practical, working knowledge of GDPR and related privacy regulation (ePrivacy or similar). Experience presenting security posture, risk, and roadmap to executives, boards, or investors. Experience building and/or managing a team — or a clear point of view on how you'd grow one as the function scales. Comfortable owning budget and vendor decisions at a strategic level, not just executing against someone else's plan. A strong cross-functional operator and executive communicator, bridging Security, IT, Legal/Privacy, Engineering, and GTM. Valued Prior experience as a Head of Security, Director of Security/IT, or similar senior/leadership title. Relevant certifications — e.g. CISSP/ISC2, CISM, AIGP, CIPP/E, CIPT, CCSK, or FIP. Experience in legal tech, AI, or another highly regulated SaaS environment. Experience designing AI risk or impact-assessment processes from scratch. Familiarity with tools such as Datagrail, MineOS, Whistic, or SafeBase. Why this role matters You'll take a senior leadership seat over security and compliance, with real ownership over how the function is shaped and grown. You'll sit at the centre of trust for a fast-growing legal AI platform, directly enabling enterprise sales and customer confidence. You'll have a clear path to building and leading a team as the function scales with the company. What you can expect A small, focused leadership group where your work has visible, immediate impact. Competitive compensation, benefits, and meaningful equity. How we work We're an in-office team in Edinburgh. We work together because it helps us collaborate closely across product, engineering, and legal teams. You should expect to be in the office as your default. This is a high ownership role. You'll be trusted to set strategy, represent security to executives and customers, and drive outcomes without heavy oversight. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

description: Group Data Protection Officer | M-KOPA Remote (covering Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa and the UK) You're the lawyer people call when a data question has no easy answer. You're accomplished. You're respected. You're probably even happy. But is your work protecting millions of people who are trusting a formal financial service with their personal information for the very first time? That is the question at the heart of this role. The trust you'd be protecting M-KOPA now serves 10 million customers, up from 5 million in 2024, and has unlocked $2+ billion in credit. 86% of our customers report an improved quality of life, 70% use our products to earn an income, and 55% are accessing products and services for the first time. Behind them stand 2,300+ employees and 35,000 agents. Every one of those customers has handed us personal information, and they did it because they believed we would handle it with care. Across Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Uganda and the UK, that belief is held under six different sets of rules, each with its own expectations about consent, retention, cross-border transfers and what happens when something goes wrong. The customers who benefit most from what we build are often the ones with the least room to absorb a mistake with their data, and that is the standard this role exists to hold. Why this timing matters You may have seen us advertising several roles across Legal, Risk and Compliance. That is deliberate, not random. We've moved from 5 million customers to 7 million, and we are now building beyond 10 million. The legal, risk and privacy foundations have to be laid ahead of that growth, not scrambled together after it. New markets, new products and new partners all arrive with new data questions. Joining now means shaping the privacy programme while its biggest chapters are still ahead of it. What makes this different In many organisations, the data protection officer reviews things at the end of the process. Here, the role reaches the whole group. Your current role: one jurisdiction, one regime. This role: six markets, one customer promise. You would report day to day to the Chief Legal, Risk and Compliance Officer, with reporting to the CEO and the Board as well. Your recommendations on strategy and implementation go to the people who run the company, and they shape how the business executes. Your work also connects directly to our mission. Financial inclusion only works if the people we serve can trust us with what they share, and you would be one of the people who keeps that trust earned. Because the role spans the whole group, you would also see patterns that no single market team can: where the same gap appears in several places, and where one fix can protect every customer at once. What you'll bring Qualified lawyer with extensive, progressive experience in data protection and privacy compliance, including running privacy operations end to end: data protection impact assessments, transfer impact assessments, vendor assessments and risk management. Detailed command of data protection law across our six markets, paired with a sound understanding of information systems, data processing operations and security needs, so you can challenge the architecture as confidently as the contract. Demonstrable experience developing policies, guidelines and template clauses for the processing of personal data, and proficiency in using AI tools responsibly to support privacy research, compliance work and risk assessment. A recognised privacy or security certification (CIPP, CIPT, or ISO 27001 or 27701 implementer or auditor) is an added advantage. It is not a gate. What you'll actually do Run the programme and fix what you find. Lead remediation and data audits, conduct DPIAs, identify where we are partially or fully non-compliant, and put it right across all six markets, while keeping the records of processing that prove it. Build the tools everyone else uses. Write the guidelines, template clauses and contracts that govern how partners, suppliers and vendors handle personal information, and support the privacy software, incident response and breach notification procedures behind them. Turn the law into culture. Design training and internal communications for staff, run awareness for third parties, and support due diligence, certification, audits and new-market expansion, so data protection is something every team does rather than something Legal does to them. The reality check This role is demanding. You will hold six regimes in your head at once, advise colleagues who would rather hear a different answer, and move a business forward with clear, plain-English advice. It is an onsite role, and your calendar will hold the strategic and the urgent in the same week: a policy redesign on Monday, a vendor assessment on Wednesday, a breach notification drill on Friday. The work rewards people who like building systems that still work when nobody is watching. You're probably ready for exactly this. Ready to build the privacy standard 10 million customers can rely on? If you read the question at the top of this page and felt something, that is probably the signal. Let's talk. Why M-KOPA? At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility. Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at m-kopa.com. Recognized four times by the Financial Times as one Africa's fastest growing companies (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026), named on CNBC's World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025 & 2026 and by TIME100 Most influential companies in the world 2023 and 2024 , we've served over 10 million customers, unlocking $2 billion in cumulative credit for the everyday earners across Africa, in addition to over 10,000 e-bikes financed in Kenya. Important Notice M-KOPA is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer committed to assembling a diverse, broadly trained staff. Women, minorities, and people with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply. M-KOPA explicitly prohibits the use of Forced or Child Labour and respects the rights of its employees to agree to terms and conditions of employment voluntarily, without coercion, and freely terminate their employment on appropriate notice. M-KOPA shall ensure that its Employees are of legal working age and shall comply with local laws for youth employment or student work, such as internships or apprenticeships. M-KOPA does not collect/charge any money as a pre-employment or post-employment requirement. This means that we never ask for ‘recruitment fees’, ‘processing fees’, ‘interview fees’, or any other kind of money in exchange for offer letters or interviews at any time during the hiring process. Applications for this position will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisting and interviews will take place at any stage during the recruitment process. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a suitable candidate is selected before the advertised closing date. If your application is successful M-KOPA undertakes pre-employment background checks as part of its recruitment process, these include; criminal records, identification verification, academic qualifications, employment dates and employer references. description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

Role Overview

This is a leadership role spearheading Nebius’s communications across Europe and the Middle East: you will develop strong regional narratives, provide senior counsel, manage and develop the team, and lead consequential communications and stakeholder situations.

Reporting to the global Head of Communications, you will translate business priorities into compelling stories and a practical regional strategy. You will connect local developments to the company narrative and adapt them to the audiences and circumstances of each market.

We need an outstanding storyteller with the gravitas, experience and judgment to personally lead high-stakes situations involving multiple stakeholders. You will know when to shape the narrative, handle a difficult relationship or lead a response yourself, and when to give colleagues the authority and support to deliver.

What success looks like

The region has clear priorities, strong narratives, credible stories and trusted stakeholder relationships. Important situations receive the right senior attention. Colleagues understand their responsibilities, exercise sound judgment and develop under your leadership. Global colleagues have early visibility of consequential regional developments.

Key Responsibilities

Shape regional narratives and strategy

  • Develop communications strategy and strong narratives for priority European and Middle Eastern markets, linked to business priorities and the wider company story.
  • Identify compelling stories and the evidence behind them. Make clear choices about audiences, markets and investment; adapt narratives locally while keeping core facts consistent.
  • Advise senior leaders on positioning, communications opportunities and reputation risks. Define measurable objectives and use evidence to improve the programme.

Lead communications and consequential stakeholder situations

  • Build trusted relationships with regional business leaders, partners and relevant business, technology, infrastructure and local media. Create a sustained pipeline of credible stories.
  • Shape and deliver the narratives, writing, executive counsel and stakeholder engagement that need your senior experience. Delegate other work with clear briefs, authority and quality standards.
  • Lead regional communications for customer, partner, product and infrastructure developments.
  • Partner with country managers and public affairs colleagues on communications and local engagement around physical infrastructure builds.

Manage people and regional resources

  • Set team priorities and responsibilities, coach colleagues, manage performance and support their development. Build the capability and confidence to make sound decisions.
  • Balance workloads and recommend where additional skills or capacity are needed. Recruit and onboard approved hires.
  • Direct agencies and partners through clear briefs, budgets and performance reviews. Judge what to own personally, what to delegate and when to intervene; retain accountability for quality and outcomes.

Coordinate across the business

  • Work closely with stakeholders across Nebius – GTM country leads, Marketing, Business Diplomacy, Product, Research, Technology, subject experts and other colleagues – to coordinate on issues including regional priorities, policy, local engagement and reputation management.
  • Coordinate with US, APAC and global communications leaders on announcements, issues and executive visibility. Maintain early visibility of consequential developments within appropriate confidentiality controls.


Key Qualifications and Experience

What we need

  • A strong record of senior communications leadership in Europe and the Middle East, with substantial in-house technology-company experience and the ability to operate credibly across the region.
  • Outstanding storytelling and narrative-development skills: translating complex business and technology priorities into compelling, credible stories for different audiences and markets.
  • Demonstrated people-management experience: setting goals, coaching, managing performance and developing capable colleagues.
  • Gravitas and senior experience to personally lead high-stakes, multi-stakeholder situations, advise business leaders and navigate competing interests with sound judgment.
  • Evidence of judging when personal involvement is essential and when to delegate, alongside strong media relationships and experience directing agencies and regional resources.
  • Outstanding English writing, editing and spoken communication, with the curiosity and rigor to understand complex technology and build accurate narratives.

Helpful experience

  • AI, cloud infrastructure, enterprise technology or another complex B2B sector; regional expansion, infrastructure investment or a publicly listed company.
  • Substantial Middle East communications work, relevant media relationships and additional regional language skills.
  • Agency experience is valuable alongside substantial in-house experience; an agency-only background does not meet the role’s requirements. Journalism experience can be beneficial.

Competencies and Behavioural Traits

Strong narrative judgment, senior presence, clear prioritisation and calm leadership. A capable people manager who develops others, gives direct feedback and delegates with purpose. Takes personal ownership where the stakes or complexity require senior experience, while keeping regional and global colleagues aligned. Comfortable with ambiguity, iteration, course-correction, experimentation and (occasionally) failure.

What We Offer

A senior communications leadership role shaping narratives and stakeholder relationships across Europe and the Middle East, working closely with business and global communications leaders and developing the regional team.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI 

Equal Opportunity Statement:

Nebius is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace and to providing equal employment opportunities in all aspects of employment. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the country in which they apply and will be required to provide proof of employment eligibility as a condition of hire. 

If you need accommodations during the application process, please let us know.

Please tell us in your application which you are applying for and what your availability and notice period are. About The AI Whistleblower Initiative (https://aiwi.org) is an independent non-profit supporting frontier AI insiders who want to raise concerns. We do this through outreach and education of insiders, access to vetted legal and financial resources, and policy work. Our insights help strengthen internal and government reporting channels, advocate for better legislation, and promote the conditions under which concerns can reach the people best placed to act on them, with source protection at their core. Find a selection of our work here (https://aiwi.org/our-work). Most high-stakes moments in AI over the coming years will involve frontier company insiders having and raising concerns: within companies, to regulators, or through other pathways. Those insiders tell us they face enormous uncertainty along the “concern raising” path -- from detecting concerns to whether and how to voice concerns with maximum impact and minimal risk, which even legally protected whistleblowing can carry. To date, no organization has dedicated itself deeply to delivering the best strategic, frontier-AI-specific guidance to these individuals, their supporters, and their attorneys (our partners). We exist to ensure that each insider disclosure is maximally impactful and safe for the person making the disclosure. Tasks About the role The Head of Security is a dual inward- and outward-facing role. You will update, design and implement AIWI’s internal security posture, and provide external guidance to AI insiders, whistleblowers and partners. You will create and oversee internal security controls, manage an evolving risk appetite, and design internal policies and trainings so that staff stay safe and secure in their everyday workflows. You will also design and deliver training and guidance to would-be whistleblowers and AIWI’s partners. In other words, you are as comfortable drafting an internal security policy or building an onboarding and device-provisioning plan as you are training whistleblowers on how to evade insider-threat-management (ITM) systems, or explaining natural language watermarking. You can design, implement, and enforce a coherent data governance policy, and you understand the intricacies of watermarking schemes and counter-forensic measures against them. You will report to Karl Koch, our CEO, and work closely with our co-founder/technical advisor Max and the principal engineer we are hiring. You will manage potential contractors and propose spend, with CEO sign-off on budget. Our environment is highly sensitive: so confidentiality, careful judgement, and conviction in what we do are essential. Areas of Ownership 1. Internal security and compliance. Onboarding, access rights, information sharing Working with trustworthy contractors Tooling: audit of all tool configurations, and keeping critical software (e.g., our GlobaLeaks instance) up to date Incident policy and response Security input and strategy on new technology and developments Full review of the current setup, identifying vulnerabilities to inform wider strategy and next steps IT helpdesking (supporting Operations to field the right ones your way) 2. External: insiders and coalition members. Guidance, video content, and op-eds Assisting coalition members Device provisioning Being “ready” to urgently support security needs Further services/offerings 3. Security engineering (full-time track only). You will build and run the technical security layer behind AIWI’s internal and external systems, working alongside the Principal Engineer (e.g. Harden and monitor our self-hosted, set up; Build security tooling, automation, and detections in-house; Review architecture and code, and secure CI/CD and the software supply chain; Run offensive testing (pen tests, red teaming) on our own systems and tools, including our GlobaLeaks instance; Lead technical incident response and forensics; Take security engineering work off the Principal Engineer so they can focus on product delivery) Requirements Core (both profiles) Experience working with and securing journalists, sources, whistleblowers, or others in high-risk sensitive environments. Proven track record of delivering security trainings to diverse audiences in a variety of environments. Demonstrated experience in source protection (how have you helped journalists or non-profits safeguard sources?). Deep knowledge of secure platforms (e.g., able to explain the security differences between Signal and SimpleX, or between Qubes and Tails). Proficiency in operational security, threat modeling, and risk management. Familiarity with IDS, ITM, and DLP suites, and how to safeguard whistleblowers against these systems. Experience drafting, enacting, and enforcing internal security controls and policies. Knowledge of document, audio, and video watermarking systems, and counter-forensics. Genuine, demonstrable commitment to AI safety and whistleblower protection. 5-15 years experience, dependent on the projects you have worked on. Additional for the full-time profile Hands-on experience as a security engineer or builder, with a track record of shipping security tooling and infrastructure. Strong coding skills in one or more of Python, Go, Rust, or C/C++, plus shell. You write security tooling, automation, and detections yourself, without relying on AI tools. Offensive security experience (penetration testing, red teaming, exploit understanding). You can think and operate like an attacker. Infrastructure security: Linux hardening, network segmentation, cloud and self-hosted setups, IaC (Ansible, OpenTofu, etc.). Application security: secure code review, OWASP Top 10, supply-chain security, secrets management. Detection and response: logging, SIEM/IDS, forensics, incident handling. Work on a vast breadth of technological challenges and varying project sizes. Ownership and responsibility from day 1. Chance to define your personal career development. Coaching by an AIWI co-founder, now board member and serial entrepreneur/CTO as well as close collaboration with an extremely experienced Principal Engineer. Joining now, you will significantly shape what the future of AI insider support looks like. We are funded until 2029. In the US, we support the federal AI Whistleblower Protection Act and have provided expert research input on implementing SB 53's incident reporting mechanisms through a research coalition, which we helped set up. Read our work in Tech Policy Press, the Institute for Law & AI, and Transformer, and see our AI Whistleblowing Law Best Practice Guide. Insider education & support: Our online campaigns have reached thousands of company employees. We produce guides (available upon request), online courses, and help establish connections to our great partner attorneys and support (e.g. on legal advice and defense funding). Network: We closely collaborate with the world's leading whistleblowing and AI organizations. Principal Account Executive — ANZ Public Sector

Why We Have This Role

We’re hiring a Principal Account Executive to lead growth across public sector and public utilities clients in ANZ from our Sydney hub. You’ll own complex, high-value opportunities that transform customer and employee experience through our SaaS XM platform, working directly with senior decision-makers (HR, marketing, executive leaders) and partnering with solutions consultants, services, marketing and customer success to design and close strategic programs.

  • Develop as a strategic partner to government and utility leaders, influencing long-term transformation programs.
  • Deepen expertise in enterprise SaaS for experience management and business transformation across public sector use cases.
  • Expand skills in negotiating large, complex deals and managing procurement & tender processes.
  • Gain visibility and influence across ANZ sales strategy and the broader product roadmap through customer insights.

  • Drive revenue and pipeline growth across ANZ public sector and utilities: prospect, qualify and close target accounts to meet and exceed revenue targets.
  • Build strategic account plans, power maps and tailored opportunity strategies, then execute demand-generation and stakeholder engagement to convert opportunities.
  • Engage and nurture stakeholders from champions to C-level, align on value and procurement timelines, and lock in long-term program outcomes.
  • Navigate public procurement and deal execution. Lead tender/RFP responses where applicable and partner with legal, finance and sales ops to remove blockers and ensure compliant contracting.
  • Lead tailored product demonstrations and craft commercial proposals with solutions consultants to maximise customer ROI and win probability.
  • Coordinate a smooth transition to customer success and services teams, track adoption and outcomes, and drive renewal and expansion opportunities.

  • 7+ years of SaaS or software sales with a strong track record of meeting/exceeding quota—experience selling enterprise or transformation solutions.

  • Experience engaging senior decision-makers in HR, marketing, executive or program leadership functions.
  • Proven ability to manage long, complex sales cycles, produce reliable forecasts and build a qualified pipeline.

  • We’re a high-performing ANZ public sector sales team focused on driving transformation through experience management technology.

  • Collaboration is central: you’ll work closely with solutions consulting, services, marketing, legal and customer success.
  • The team invests in development and promotes on performance—expect coaching, stretch targets and visible career progression.
  • Working here gives exposure to meaningful public-sector outcomes that impact large populations and communities.

  • Salary + uncapped commissions and accelerators.
  • Performance-based promotions—advancement driven by results.
  • Private health insurance with comprehensive medical and extras coverage.

  • Hybrid working (typically 3 days in office / 2 from home) and commuter allowance.
  • Catered lunches and a well-stocked kitchen at our North Sydney office.

description: quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app. quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end. Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll. The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters. Where this is going Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either. That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience. One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy. Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled. Why this role exists Today, quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with. What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards. That is the opening. How we work We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing. We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way. And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high. Tasks What you will own Everything on the screen: The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account. The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components. The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device. Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native. The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished. Where design ends, engineering begins. We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you. Requirements Who we are looking for You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed. You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building. You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels. You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does. Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works. The Team We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action. This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally. Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.
